report.summary: Chunk 4 of 5 of canary.py: defines default_lanes, LiveCanaryRefused, _adapters_behind, live_egress_lanes, grade, _run_lane, run_canary, _new_run_id, dry_run_plan. Claims about fail-closed, single classifier, sequential per-lane, live opt-in, etc. are kept; some claims are uncheckable.
risks: _adapters_behind | medium | Uses `cell.cell_contents` inside try/except ValueError to handle empty cells. If a closure cell contains a non-adapter that raises a different exception (e.g., AttributeError), it will propagate and crash. | Add broader exception handling or check cell_contents type before accessing.

grade | medium | When reply.status != 'ok', the function accesses `reply.reason`, `reply.stderr`, and `reply.content` without checking if they exist. If the VendorReply class does not guarantee these attributes, an AttributeError may occur. | Ensure VendorReply has these attributes or use getattr with defaults.

run_canary | low | The `thread.join(max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))` may join with a negative timeout if deadline has passed; max ensures non-negative, but the join may return immediately, leaving threads running as daemons. This is by design but could lead to incomplete results. | Document that threads are daemons and abandoned at wall clock.
dry_run_plan | uncheckable | The docstring claims 'Calls nothing -- no lane.ask is touched' but the function body is not in this chunk. | Review the full function definition.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY, per call. ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is neither read for routing nor written anywhere here
claims.why: The function takes `ollama_host` as a parameter and uses it; there is no reference to an environment variable OLLAMA_HOST in this chunk.

claims.text: the ``local`` flag is a property of the RESOLVED host rather than of the provider's name: the bench is another machine, so a probe sent there is egress and is labelled as such on every record it produces.
claims.why: For 'local' vendor, lane is set to 'trusted' if _is_local_http(host) else 'untrusted', and the Lane's 'local' field is set from `getattr(a, 'local', False)`, which depends on the adapter's 'local' attribute, not the vendor name.

claims.text: A lane that can reach a real vendor was offered without ``live=True``.
claims.why: The class is raised in run_canary when live=False and live_egress_lanes returns non-empty seats.

claims.text: Subclasses the council's refusal ON PURPOSE. "You were about to spend money" is one catchable family across this package; a caller that wants to treat both the same writes ``except LiveCouncilRefused`` and cannot miss one of them by having been written before the other existed.
claims.why: The class inherits from LiveCouncilRefused, so except LiveCouncilRefused catches both.

claims.text: Every :class:`CouncilAdapter` a lane's ``ask`` could actually reach.
claims.why: The function checks lane.adapter, ask.__self__, and ask.__closure__ cells for CouncilAdapter instances.

claims.text: Three places, because :func:`default_lanes` is not the only way to build a :class:`Lane` and a gate that only understood that one path would be a gate with a documented bypass
claims.why: The function checks three places: adapter field, __self__, and __closure__, covering hand-rolled Lanes.

claims.text: Finding NOTHING means ``ask`` is a plain caller-supplied callable, and the verdict for that is deliberately the same one :func:`session.live_egress_seats` already gives an unrecognised class: it is the caller's own code and the caller owns it.
claims.why: The behavior of live_egress_seats when given an empty tuple is not defined in this chunk; the claim about the verdict cannot be verified.

If live_egress_seats returns an empty tuple, the function returns an empty tuple, meaning no lanes are considered egress. This is fail-closed because any unrecognized adapter is not considered egress.

claims.text: The classification itself is NOT done here -- it is :func:`session.live_egress_seats`, imported.
claims.why: The function calls live_egress_seats (imported) to classify adapters.

claims.text: The checker runs ONLY on ``status == "ok"``: grading the body of a reply we never received would manufacture a ``wrong_answer`` out of an outage, which is the same lie as merging the two statuses.
claims.why: The function checks `if reply.status != "ok":` and returns early with a transport error status; only when status is 'ok' does it call probe.check.

claims.text: Sequential within a lane on purpose: four concurrent calls to the same vendor is a load test, not a health check, and it would make the latency numbers -- the thing the trailing median compares -- meaningless. It is also what keeps a hung vendor to ONE occupied slot rather than four.
claims.why: The function iterates over probes sequentially in a for loop, not concurrently.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are ABANDONED at the wall clock rather than joined: a thread cannot be killed, so a hung vendor must degrade the report instead of blocking it.
claims.why: Threads are created with `daemon=True` (line not shown but implied), and the main thread only joins with a timeout: `thread.join(max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))`.

claims.text: Every abandoned (lane, probe) is still reported -- as ``timeout``/``wall_clock`` -- because a silently dropped row is indistinguishable from a probe that was never scheduled.
claims.why: After joining, for each (lane, probe, box) in plan, if box.get('result') is None, a ProbeResult with status 'timeout' and reason 'wall_clock' is created and appended to results.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False. Any lane that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_lanes`) raises :class:`LiveCanaryRefused` here -- before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched, and therefore before there is anything for :func:`append_history` to write.
claims.why: The function checks `if not live:` early, calls `live_egress_lanes(lanes)`, and raises LiveCanaryRefused if seats is non-empty, before any threads are started.

claims.text: Fake lanes are unaffected, so the offline harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The function only raises if live_egress_lanes returns non-empty; fake lanes with no real adapters will result in an empty tuple, so no exception.

observations.what: The docstring of _adapters_behind makes a claim about the behavior of live_egress_seats for unrecognized classes, but that function is not defined in this chunk.
The docstring of dry_run_plan claims it calls nothing, but the function body is not present; the claim is uncheckable.
In grade, when reply.status != 'ok', the code accesses reply.reason, reply.stderr, and reply.content without checking for existence, assuming they are attributes of VendorReply.
In _adapters_behind, the try/except only catches ValueError for empty cells; other exceptions from cell.cell_contents (e.g., AttributeError if cell is not a proper cell) would propagate.
